directions.name: Demand
directions.question: What developments change the scale or timing of customer demand and deployment for NVIDIA systems?
directions.source_quote: From hyperscalers to model makers to AI cloud providers and sovereign customers.

directions.name: Supply
directions.question: What developments change the availability, costs or constraints of inputs and infrastructure for NVIDIA systems?
directions.source_quote: increased total supply inclusive of inventory purchase commitments on prepaids to $145 billion

directions.name: Competition
directions.question: What developments change NVIDIA competition, substitute products, or market share?
directions.source_quote: if deployed on our competitors’ platforms, it could reduce demand for our products and services.

directions.name: Pricing
directions.question: What developments change NVIDIA products pricing or the useful life of installed systems?
directions.source_quote: The price of renting an H100 has risen 20% year to date, while A100 cloud pricing is up nearly 15%.

directions.name: Product rollout
directions.question: What developments change the timing, deployment or capability of NVIDIA product generations?
directions.source_quote: Starting this year, AWS will add more than 1 million Blackwell and Rubin GPUs

directions.name: Policy
directions.question: What policy or approval changes affect NVIDIA product access, sales or supply?
directions.source_quote: the US government has approved licenses for H200 to be shipped to China based customers

directions.name: Capital
directions.question: What financing, guarantees and supply obligations could affect NVIDIA and its ecosystem?
directions.source_quote: facility lease guarantees, long-term debt, purchase commitments, and operating lease obligations
